I was heavily bullied. Whether it be my weight, hair, hygiene, tastes in music, behaviour blah blah blah, the reasons didn't really matter. What mattered was that I made myself an easy target. Alot of my issues stemmed from a lack of self worth and self confidence that was developed independently of the bullying. My mother would tell me 'listen I know it hurts just wait one more year and you'll be out of school, be brave everything will be OK' that does not help at all

I rejected that same stupid advice I'd gotten all through school. In my last year started to believe in myself. To love myself, take care of my body and hold my head high. I stuck up for myself, even if it did get me punched a few times (I was a pacifist but I stood my ground, I didn't back down). It was having self worth that saved me from the bullying. I didn't wait for school to stop, I stopped the bullying myself.

Something like your sexuality, your parents etc doesn't matter. It is how you handle the bullies.

The best example of this I know is that there were only 2 openly gay lads at my school. One was timid and shy and scared. The other was the queen of comebacks, sassy, sporty, active and funny.

The timid one was tortured and bullied and did not have a great time, the sassy one shot down all insults perfectly and was untouchable. He used to be quiet and shy himself, but after he came out of the closet he changed completely, and became one of the more popular kids in school. It's about being true to yourself, and standing up for yourself.

I'm sorry for the rambling post. I guess what I'm saying is that you should never tell your child to be someone they're not just to avoid bullying, that is not going to help. Improving your kids health and hygiene should be something the child does for themselves and nobody else.

I look at it as, had someone told me how to behave better, how to socialize more normally, I think I'd have been much better off. I learned it the hard way and started fighting back as I got older so people stopped messing with me, but if someone had guided me earlier and said 'don't do xyz', 'make sure you brush your hair', etc., I truly think I'd have had a much better childhood. Instead I was alone and miserable. I learned to fit in more as I got older and it helped tremendously, but I learned it on my own and learned it much later than most kids and in the end I was much angrier and more resentful than the other kids. I wish I'd had someone to tell me how to act, what to say, how to make and keep friends, etc. I guess that is just my own perspective on it.

I think our perspectives are not mutually exclusive. The parenting you are suggesting would have made it a lot easier for me to deal with my bullies. Fixing the things that can be fixed, and fighting for the things that make you who you are.

Basically. I mean if my kid said they absolutely felt that they needed to do xyz because it made them feel complete or something, I wouldn't force them not to, I'd just tell them that they were probably going to have to face bullies and if so, here's how to deal with them. I never fought with fists except once or twice but for the most part, I was like the gay guy you described - I'd have a retort for everything so everyone kinda gave up and let me be.

Edit: I also want to just say that it's nice to talk to someone who is willing to have a calm discussion. It seems so rare these days. Thank you.
